1947, February 27
The following is a faithful transcription of the typed original by the Servant of God, Father Solanus Casey, O.P.M. Cap. (A carbon copy mailed to Mr. & Mrs. J. J. 0'Donnell)
COPY Mr. M.C.Costello. Hargill, Texas.
February 27th 1947. St. Felix Friary Huntington, Ind.
My Dear Mr. Costello: God bless you and yours. The O'Donnells told me several weeks ago that you were writing me -- having told me quite allittle about you for several past months. Only just now did I come across your interesting letter of February 26th -- somehow mislaid -- that I've been looking for. So I am not keeping you in any possible suspence as to my identity, interest, etc.
You ask about Appleton, Wisconsin. It was in St.Joseph's Church in that neat little city where I had my first Holy Mass, July 31st 1904. God be blessed.Deo Gr. No. I can not say that I am exactly from St. Paul, Minn; though many a pleasant day I spent in that thrifty city - with relatives and friends and in the Seminary, as guest.
Coming two years in June, on my way to Seattle, I visited an old friend of mine Mike Costello who had been moldest brother's bare-foot-boy friend on our farms sixty-five years before and about forty miles down the River on the Wisconsin side. Later, when I was about 17, I did a term in the Stillwater Penetentiary (less thantwo months), and I found Mike there ahead of me and we became bed-fellows - he a boiler-maker and his partner just "a roustabout". However, we had our sleeping-quarters outside the wall.
Some years after that the one became a lieutenant in the Saint Paul police- department; the other a poor Capuchin and a priest. Mike was in his 80s and wasalmost hlind when we went to see hm on said trip - seemingly rejuvanited at our visit. Ihhad spoken to him on the phone a number of times but for over thirty years had not seen him. So that, when our O'Donnell Friends seemed disapointed several weeks back I felt there must be a mistake or a misunderstanding "in the woodpile" somewhere. Thanks be to God for all interested it turned out to be so, - just another blessing in disguise I trust. For I feel that as you learn to know these friends, as I have known them for several years, you will come to feel that you are rather working with them than just for them. Indeed I hope such feeling of confidence may become generously mutual between you.
God bless you all again. Sincerely Yours in Christ, Fr. Solanus, 0 FM.Cap.
Best regards to the Conley group. Pl pardon brevity.
Praised be Jesus Christ. Fr. Solanus
